analysis.title: "We're All Rudderless": Goldman's Trading Floor Maps The AI Unwind, Either "Cut CapEx, Delay, Or Dilute"
key_insights: Goldman's Rich Privorotsky frames the AI selloff as a repricing of the cost of capital, not a demand problem. The assumption of unlimited cheap capital to fund the buildout is being challenged, and the options are cut capex, delay deployment or fund through equity. He says the underlying demand picture hasn't really changed.

On Thursday AI stocks had their worst day relative to the S&P ex-AI since the DeepSeek moment, even after Meta beat on ads and Western Digital gave a roughly 20% EPS guidance beat and raise. WDC reversed from +4% to -8%, and Bloom Energy slid on cash conversion despite a strong quarter.

Meta's future spending commitments rose to $825bn from roughly $700bn in July, per Goldman's Sean Johnstone. Meta has negative free cash flow, a higher spending floor and an explicit equity-financing vehicle. Its five-year CDS hit a record, Oracle's stayed near highs and Microsoft's widened.

The WSJ flagged roughly $3trn of off-balance-sheet AI commitments, including $1.2trn of leases. ZeroHedge's own tally of hyperscaler off-balance-sheet debt is $3.6trn as of Oct 21 and it expects the total to cross $4trn when the remaining companies report.

Goldman's Gabriela Borges estimates CoreWeave needs about $38bn to ramp its secured 4.2GW and about $23bn in new debt for current contracts, roughly $61bn in total against a potential $260bn backlog. That is close to Bernstein's $76bn funding gap estimate. Oracle RPO rose to $664bn from $455bn, and the OCI gross-profit inflection is likely within 12 months.
Nebius secured a $3.5bn financing facility, so funding is still available. The facility is short-dated and does not resolve longer-term funding needs.

Credit has moved through Goldman's downside case. USD HY closed Thursday at 338bp versus the 335bp downside-scenario peak, at the 100th percentile of the past year. IG is at 87bp versus the 93bp downside level. CCC spreads are at 1,111bp, up 313bp in three months and the widest in three years. Amanda Lynam now expects spreads to moderately overshoot those ranges, with risks tilted to more widening before year-end.

Hedge funds had a broad loss day. Over two-thirds finished down, and for the first time since COVID all three equity strategies fell more than 1% on the same day. Fundamental L/S fell 1.4%, TMT-focused funds fell 2.7% (-9.6% MTD), systematic L/S fell 1.3% and multi-strats fell 1.9%.

Unconstrained momentum is suffering its worst drawdown since the GFC outside COVID, per Privorotsky. The unwind spilled from long/short funds into systematic funds. Goldman's HF Positioning Pair fell about 4.2%, its worst move since 2011 and -10.4% MTD. The High Beta Momentum pair has erased all YTD gains after a 43% drawdown.

The SOX has underperformed the S&P by 13% over nine sessions, its worst stretch in more than 20 years, though it still leads by 40% YTD. Five-day moves in Goldman's AI baskets: NeoClouds -14.6%, Optical Networks -12.2%, Memory -10.0%, Data Centers -9.1%. AI-at-Risk was +7.1%.

Under the surface it looked like a liquidation. The S&P fell 121bps and the Nasdaq 100 fell 290bps, yet 335 S&P names closed higher and equal-weight RSP closed near its highs, up 68bps. The gap between breadth and price was the widest since DeepSeek Monday and the second widest since at least 1990.

Goldman's derivatives desk called Thursday a capitulation and de-grossing, but VIX was 18.49, the market-on-close imbalance was $6.2bn to buy, volume was barely above the YTD average and the floor activity scale read 5 of 10. Net exposure has fallen without a similar fall in gross (213.9%, 83rd percentile over three years), leaving crowded long/short momentum trades vulnerable. Japan gross is in the 92nd percentile.

Three Goldman notes pitched momentum drawdowns as attractive entry points with limited-loss structures. The median 3-month return after a 10% momentum drawdown is +16.4%. The two 2026 episodes were weaker: the March dip worked for three months and then gave it back, and the July dip fell another 15.4% the following month.

Treasuries rallied. The 10Y fell about 15bps Thursday, the largest one-day move since August 2025, and the 10Y at 4.95% is still in the 99th percentile since 2010. The Fed curve still prices nearly 3 hikes. Privorotsky says the rate rally depends on AI hurting, and if AI stabilizes rates could come under pressure again. The 10Y was back at 4.97% Friday morning.

Brent hit $114 Friday morning. Privorotsky says headline signaling has already delivered much of the price impact of a disruption, leaving the risk premium exposed to a sell-the-news unwind. He also flags high-severity software vulnerabilities running at roughly ten times the 2022-25 pace.

Korea's Kospi fell more than 4% early Friday and closed up 0.3%, which Goldman's trader found encouraging. Goldman saw buy tickets mostly in industrials and large CoreWeave upside buying in derivatives. Kaplan saw zero signs of offense on AI, with hedge funds 10% better for sale and ETF shorts outpacing long sales 2 to 1. Near-record short leverage makes a squeeze possible.

Next week's hyperscaler results are the test, specifically how backlog converts to revenue, the pace of deployment and what companies say about funding. ZeroHedge argues that if this is a cost-of-capital story, a strong guide will not fix it.

tension_points.bull_case: Demand for AI remains robust per Goldman's Privorotsky. Buyers are emerging in industrials and CoreWeave upside, Korea stabilized, and near-record short leverage makes a violent squeeze possible.
tension_points.bear_case: The cost of cheap capital is being repriced, with Meta CDS at a record, HY through Goldman's downside case and about $3trn+ of off-balance-sheet commitments. Gross exposure remains high so momentum unwinds can continue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Next week's hyperscaler results: backlog-to-revenue conversion, deployment pace and funding commentary.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman notes call momentum drawdowns attractive entry points, with a median 3-month return of +16.4% after a 10% drawdown.
tension_points.bear_case: The March 2026 dip gave back its gains after three months and the July dip fell another 15.4% in the following month.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Gross exposure falling meaningfully from the 83rd percentile, or a further slide of the momentum factor below the July trough.

tension_points.bull_case: Bonds are working as a hedge, with the AI selloff doing some of the tightening work and the 10Y falling 15bps.
tension_points.bear_case: If AI stabilizes and growth expectations recover, rates could come under pressure again, and the Fed curve still prices nearly 3 hikes with the 10Y in the 99th percentile since 2010.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 10Y moving back above Thursday's 4.95% close, as it did to 4.97% Friday morning.
